text:
acme-dev: Hey team — after we cut over the transport to our VPC and added a new subnet that overlaps our on-prem CIDR, calls to Redwood's API are intermittently failing. curl shows TLS handshake errors (SSL_connect: certificate verify failed). Started ~0900 UTC.
support-anna: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a quick repro (curl + dig/nslookup) and confirm whether you're hitting our hosted endpoint or a PrivateLink/VPC endpoint?
acme-dev: Repro below. We see DNS sometimes resolving to 10.2.3.4 (private) and sometimes to public IPs. Happening from hosts in the new subnet only.

$ dig +short api.redwood.example.com
10.2.3.4
52.14.23.11

$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (10.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* Server certificate: CN=fw-proxy.local
* SSL_connect error: certificate verify failed

jordan: That looks like split-horizon/resolver differences + a TLS intercept/proxy in path. Two things to check quickly: (1) whether the VPC endpoint's Private DNS is enabled for your account (if you created a cross-account endpoint, private DNS could be disabled), and (2) route table path — traffic to 10.2.3.4 should hit the VPC endpoint ENI, not be routed to TGW/NAT/onsite proxy.
mika: Also check the endpoint ENI security group and source/dest check on the ENI. If there's an egress proxy/firewall doing TLS-inspect it will replace certs with its own and you'll get that CN. From an instance in the subnet run:

# list VPC endpoints in the VPC
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0abcd1234 --query 'VpcEndpoints[*].[VpcEndpointId,ServiceName,PrivateDnsEnabled]' --output table

# map ENI -> private ip
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0123456789abcdef --query 'VpcEndpoints[0].NetworkInterfaceIds'
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --network-interface-ids eni-0aaaa111 --query 'NetworkInterfaces[0].PrivateIpAddresses'

# quick tcptrace
sudo tcpdump -ni eth0 host 10.2.3.4 and port 443 -w /tmp/vpce.pcap

sre-liz: Another pattern I've seen: on-prem DNS forwarders conditionally return on-prem private IPs for the same hostname when requests come from the on-prem resolver; then your VPC resolver (Route53 resolver inbound endpoints) forwards to on-prem and gets the on-prem IP back — causes hairpin to your firewall that does TLS-inspect. If the cidr overlap caused your resolver rules to forward queries for the zone to on-prem, you'll see inconsistent answers.
support-anna: TL;DR checklist for customer to run: 1) From an affected host: dig +short api.redwood.example.com @169.254.169.253 (VPC resolver) and dig @<onprem-dns> — compare. 2) Confirm Route Table: the subnet's route for the endpoint prefix must be local (the VPC endpoint creates ENI routes automatically). 3) Check the outbound path: if traffic leaves the VPC (TGW/NAT) then firewall may be intercepting TLS. 4) Capture pcap and attach.

acme-dev: Results: VPC resolver -> 10.2.3.4, on-prem -> 10.2.3.4 as well (so on-prem authoritative), but traceroute shows first hop to our perimeter FW when we hit the private IP. So DNS is returning private host and traffic is traversing to our firewall (via TGW) not staying local to the endpoint ENI.
jordan: That implies a routing preference issue: check the subnet route table that hosts use (ip route get 10.2.3.4) and also check interface association for endpoint ENIs — if the ENI is in different AZ or account, ensure the endpoint's policy allows your VPC traffic and that there are no conflicting explicit routes to TGW for that CIDR.
mika: Quick workaround: disable on-prem conditional forwarder for that zone or add a Route 53 inbound rule that returns the endpoint IPs locally; long-term either ensure the resolver chain returns the endpoint IP only for queries routed inside the VPC, or create an endpoint in the account+subnet where the callers live (and enable Private DNS).
sre-liz: If you can't change DNS quickly, you can force curl to use the public IP to test if TLS succeeds:

curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:52.14.23.11 https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/health

That should bypass the private path and prove whether TLS is ok to our public host.

acme-dev: Doing that now — public path succeeds and returns 200 OK. So confirms TLS-inspect on the private path. We'll update our resolver rules and work with infra to patch the TGW route priority.

support-anna: Great. If you want, provide the vpce id and we'll confirm the endpoint service side and share the service zone IDs so you can pin DNS responses. Also attach the pcap and traceroute when ready. We can escalate to infra if you need help disabling the conditional forwarder. :thumbsup:

redwood-deploy-bot: Reminder — if you need us to verify endpoint service details, include account id and vpce id; sharing logs over support ticket will keep this traceable.

acme-dev: Thanks — opening a ticket with vpce-0123456789abcdef, account 123456789012 and attaching pcaps. Will update when resolver rules are changed.
support-anna: Thanks — leaving this thread open until you confirm. Happy to validate after change. :white_check_mark:
